1955 — 1960 TUBE COMBO

Tweed
Deluxe.

The little amp that learned
to roar.

In 1955, Fender gave the Deluxe a narrow-panel cabinet and the 5E3 circuit—a modest amplifier built for working musicians. Its pair of 6V6 power tubes delivered warm cleans that gave way to thick, compressed overdrive as the volume climbed. Neil Young made the tweed Deluxe part of his unmistakable electric voice. The secret wasn’t more power: it was what happened when this small amp reached its limits.

THE CHARACTERWarm. Raw. Beautifully unruly.
